1	import { PHASE_PRODUCTION_BUILD } from "next/constants";
2	
3	/**
4	 * Detects if the application is in build phase (SSG/static generation).
5	 * During build phase, we bypass internal API proxy and call external API directly
6	 * to avoid issues when the Next.js server isn't running.
7	 *
8	 * This is used to determine whether to use internal API routes (runtime) or
9	 * external API calls (build time) for data fetching.
10	 *
11	 * NEXT_PHASE is the only reliable signal — it's set by the Next.js CLI itself
12	 * during `next build`, regardless of hosting platform. A `NODE_ENV ===
13	 * "production" && !VERCEL_URL` fallback used to be OR'd in here, added when
14	 * this app only ran on Vercel (VERCEL_URL is always set at Vercel runtime, so
15	 * its absence meant "must be the build step"). Since the Coolify migration,
16	 * that assumption is false: self-hosted production never sets VERCEL_URL
17	 * either, so the fallback made isBuildPhase permanently true at runtime,
18	 * silently bypassing the internal API's caching/revalidation for places,
19	 * regions, cities, categories, and events on every production request.
20	 *
21	 * Lives in its own module (not utils/constants.ts) so the API data-fetching
22	 * layer (lib/api/regions.ts, cities.ts, places.ts, events.ts, categories.ts)
23	 * doesn't transitively pull in next-intl/server and the full ca/es/en message
24	 * bundles just to read one boolean flag.
25	 */
26	export const isBuildPhase = process.env.NEXT_PHASE === PHASE_PRODUCTION_BUILD;
